properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8260074
Permit API: 117-20391
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Jackson Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/29/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Barrett 410 well pad located in Jackson Township, Tioga County on 12/29/2025 at 1025 hours. The weather was 41 degrees F with mostly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator.On 12/24/2025, Repsol reported to the DEP via the reporting hotline that an estimated 23 gallons of produced fluids were released to the soil/gravel after the dump line for the produced fluids separated. Repsol reported that the impacted soil/gravel was recovered and that a third party company would visit on Friday, 12/26/2025, to verify that cleanup was complete. During my inspection, evidence of remediation was observed off the western fill slope (photo #6). Impacted materials were placed in a lined and covered residual waste container stored onsite (photo #2). The dump line appears to have a temporary repair in place (photo #5) with tape over the damage line. A bucket is located below the line to collect any additional leaks. Repsol reported that a permanent repair is scheduled for the near future. Any fluids and soils in and around the remediated area showed no evidence of any portion of the release remaining. Based on the findings of this inspection report, the reported release of produced fluids outside of secondary containment and Repsol's timely remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-20391:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)SWMA 301I departed the site at 1135 hours.

Permit API: 065-27128
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/24/2026
Comments: Administrative review of documents associated with the plug and skid event of the David Weaver #1 (065-27128) well. Spud of new borehole commenced on 05/28/2026. Required documents were received by the Department on 06/16/2026. Section 3211(f)(6) of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act requires the submission of these documents within 10 days of the commencement of the new borehole. Eighteen days had elapsed since the commencement of the new well and the submission of the required documents. Parts of the required documentation were found to be administratively incomplete. The well record submission did not contain the log of formations and freshwater shows, as required by Section 78.122(a)(9), of Title 25 PA Code Chapter 78 Oil and Gas Wells The certificate of well plugging did not contain information pertaining to the plug depths and materials, as well as the pipe sizes and depths that were left in the well. This information is required under section 78.124(b) of Title 25 PA Code, Chapter 78 Oil and Gas Wells. Operator will be required to submit the information which was omitted in the previous submission. Appropriate Notice of Violations (NOV's) have been documented in this inspection report. Inadequate operator submissions will be made a part of the report and will be available within the Department database.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 992328
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-05-31
Violation Code: SWMA 610(4) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person stored, collected, transported, processed, treated, beneficially used or disposed of, or assisted in the storage, collection, transportation, processing, treatment, or disposal of, solid waste contrary to the rules or regulations adopted under the Solid Waste Management Act, or orders of DEP, or terms or conditions of a permit, or in a manner creating a public nuisance or which adversely affected the public health, safety and welfare.
Violation ID: 851803
Permit API: 051-23818
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Luzerne Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-05-31
Comments: On 5/31/19 a follow up inspection of the Waters 10 Well Site was conducted accompanied by WQS Supervisor John Carson in response to issues noted in a prior inspection. The following was observed: >>The well equipment and site appeared unchanged from the previous inspection. >>The production/brine tank remained in poor condition with visible seepage from the rust holes in the tanks lower end. In response to the initial inspection the operator stated that the tank had not been used and that the well produced no brine. At the time of the inspection the tank held roughly 10-20" of cloudy fluid and dead vegetation on the earth work around it indicated a ground plume of contamination. This piece of equipment can no longer serve as a tank or appropriate storage device for production fluids. Immediate replacement of failed equipment and removal of impacted materials recommended. This constitutes a violation of SWMA 401(A), 610(4), 25 Pa. Code § 78.54, and 25 Pa. Code § 78.57(a) in that the operator failed to store hazardous waste in accordance with the rules and regulations of the DEP resulting in conditions hazardous to public health and safety and a failure to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. A site characterization is necessary to assess the extent of impact and appropriate action to remedy contamination. >>Gravel and other debris remained sloughed onto the public roadway and continue to indicate substantial runoff from the site during rain events. This constitutes a violation of 25 Pa. Code 102.11(a)(1) in that the operator failed to successfully design, implement, and maintain site BMPs.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/18/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 962250
Permit API: 081-20531
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response from a notification from the operator that on July 18, 2022, an unknown volume of brine, mixed with oil and stormwater, had overflowed the secondary containment. I met with Rick Hall of EQT upon arriving on location. Tobias excavation was also present on location as well as Creston Environmental. A coiled tubing unit and associated equipment was present on the pad on secondary containment. Damp areas and puddles were present on the north and south sides of the containment. Rick Hall said that the fluid made it off of the containment on both sides. On the north side of the containment the electrical conductivity (EC) in the puddles as measured by the Oakton meter ranged from 651 uS/cm to 3.16 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment each puddle I measured had an EC of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. Toward the end of my inspection, personnel on location had removed a portion of the containment berm on the north side and pulled back the liner approximately 15 feet which revealed that the gravel under the containment was damp. I would estimate the area visibly impacted by the release at approximately 600 square feet.Rick Hall said that the coiled tubing crew should be done by Thursday, July 21st, and then the containment would be removed from the pad surface. Screening of the pad surface where the containment was present would occur at that time, according to Rick Hall. Due to the unknown volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.Violations noted.

Violation ID: 8226205
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/20/2025
Comments: On March 20, 2025, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Kriebel Natural Gas Co's RWS Development 001 Well located in Manor Borough, Westmoreland County in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Accompanying on today's inspection was Kriebel representative's Ben Dickun and Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Dickun and Mr. Seich stated that the production tank on site had been emptied prior to our arrival on site and that they were going to install booms in the ditch that runs adjacent to the well site and terminates at a nearby stream downslope. The DEP inquired whether any other remediation efforts were going to be conducted while the DEP was on site or after the inspection, and Mr. Dickun stated that they were awaiting instruction from the DEP. At the time of this inspection, the DEP verbally recommended Kriebel promptly remediate the brine release in accordance with Act 2 protocol. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.During IR 3941481 and 3941519, the DEP collected several soil conductivity readings around the well site to determine the extent of the release and concluded that the brine release was contained to a ditch that runs alongside the well site edge and terminates just before a stream. No elevated conductivity readings were collected in the stream, therefore at the time of that inspection, it did not appear that there were any impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).At the time of this inspection, the DEP took a background soil conductivity upslope and away from the incident area (0.0833 mS), and then soil conductivity readings were taken within the ditch: Right by the production equipment (1.225 mS and 1.105 mS), right by a inlet that appeared to be plugged with rocks and plastic (1.165 mS), right by an outlet that appeared to be dry at the time of this inspection (0.828 mS), and then in the ditch leading up to where it terminates just before the stream (1.132 mS, 1.236 mS, and 1.348 mS,). Readings taken directly upslope of the ditch on both sides were comparable to the background reading, while readings taken inside the ditch were elevated, subjugating that the release still appears to be contained to the ditch. To determine whether the stream had become impacted from the brine release, at the time of this inspection, a soil conductivity readings was taken on the stream bank directly downslope of where the ditch terminates (0.593 mS), then a soil (0.402 mS) and fluid (0.459 mS) conductivity reading was taken in the stream directly downslope of where the ditch terminates and lastly, a fluid reading was taken upslope (0.527 mS) and downslope (0.524 mS) of this area. Based on the DEP's observations and these conductivity readings, it appears that the WOC at the time of this inspection remain unscathed from the brine release. Permit API: 003-22234
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/06/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/27/2020 as well as a follow up to a previously reported spill from 8/15/2020 which has been reported as remediated. The operator reported that the spill occurred at approximately 9:30 PM when a check valve washed out. The operator reported approximately 1 barrel of Production Fluid was discharged to the ground. When asked via phone on 12/28/2020, Mr. Hardy reported that the operator would remediate the spill in accordance with Act 2. The following is observed: The Act 9 Sign is present, the ERP, PPC, and associated SDS are in the mailbox adjacent (Photo 1). The operator has removed material between GPUs 2H and 3H (Photo 2) thereby constructing a sump approximately a foot and a half deep and nearly the length of the GPU (Photo 11). Background readings taken in the area were between 70 uS and 300 uS (Photo 12 & 13). Readings taken in the vicinity of standing water in the sump were between 2,000 uS and 13,500 uS. Readings of 2,000 uS were detected between the skids of GPU 3H (Photo 16 & 17). GPU 3H is attached to GPU 16H, on the other side of this structure between another piece of Production Equipment was another smaller "sump" (Photo 6). Background in this area was around 500 uS (Photo 7). Readings taken around this sump were detected at 7,000 uS to 13,000 uS (Photo 5 & 8). GPUs 3H and 16H do not appear to have adequate secondary containment. Per the CO&A entered into on 12/17/2020, these are noted as ICS. The Department requests information on how the operator is going to remediate the impacted material in accordance with 91.33(B) and submit it before 1/11/21. Additionally, the Department requests more information on how the discharge reached the other side of 16H and how the operator intends to remediate any impacted material below the GPUs. The Department requests information on how the amount spilled was quantified. The Department also requests a copy of the waste manifest once it is available. In reference to the 8/15/2020 spill, it appears that sump has been back filled (Photo 19). The Department requests documentation including photographs of the remediation effort prior to filling in the excavated area and including conductivity readings adjacent to and under the GPU. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground associated with GPU 3H. Violations associated with the spill that occurred on 8/15/2020 and referenced in IR 3096843 will remain outstanding. Pending the operators response, further violations may be issued.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 885881
Permit API: 081-21803
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-06-02
Comments: On June 2, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection as a response to a reported production fluid spill at Beech Resources Premier Pad. DEP received a phone call from Don Stevenson with Beech Resources reporting a spill of around 400 gallons of production fluid from the GPU onsite. A dump line valve on the GPU recently failed and was replaced. Within the next couple days vegetation downslope from the GPU was noticed to be dead. How the production fluid was spilled is still being determined. At the time of the inspection, the operator was in the process of excavating the impacted soil. There are two strips of impacted soil, they are about equal in size. The impacted area is about 10 ft wide by 90 ft long. At the top of the slope, the excavator had dug up about 3 ft deep of soil. Soil conductivity in the right strip of dead vegetation ranged from 700 uS/cm to over range readings of the meter, which is 4,000 uS/cm. The impacted soil is still within the LOD so no production fluid left the permitted LOD. Beech Resources plans to follow the Act 2 remediation. The spill of production fluid outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Outstanding violations from Inspection No. 3001824 still remain.

No waterways were impacted by the release and no apparent migration of the material was observed. Two roll off waste disposal boxes were on site to collect the impacted material for disposal. The Operator is in compliance with the current Department spill policy for reporting the release. Violations area being issued for the release.

Violation ID: 8267123

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tank, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time.The Department obtained soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank near the corroded piping. Readings of 0.74ms, 0.42mS, 0.56mS, were obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading obtained of 0.09mS. It does not appear any remediation has occurred on site at the time of this inspection.Soil conductivity readings under the pipe were collected in the same localized location during the Department's previous inspection documented in IR 4106039 where it was 1.285mS. Therefore, since neither evidence of remedial actions were observed, nor a response from the operator has been received, the violations for a release remain outstanding as it appears the release may be diluting and/or migrating into the surrounding soil/subsurface areas.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 2/14/20 an incident inspection of the Beacon well pad was conducted in response to a spill (CTS ID: 347983) reported on 2/10/20. The following was observed: >>On 2/11/20 WQSS John Carson spoke with Greylock Representative Keith Eighmey who reported that while drilling using a filming agent foam from an open topped tank blew to the well pad and via a failed seam in the pad containment traveled to the pad's drainage ditches and then to the primary sediment basin and into the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC; unnamed tributary to Frosty Run). The amount of material lost was reported as unknown but minimal. Operator sampling and MSDS were requested. >>At the time of inspection the sediment basin was found to be overflowing via the stand pipe resulting in substantial flow of sediment laden waters bypassing and flowing through site perimeter controls causing accelerated erosion and impact to the WOC. Additionally, the runoff stream and channel off site notably still bore multiple large piles of foam strongly indicating ongoing impact related to the reported spill. At the time of inspection dewatering/pumping out the impacted water from the sediment basin and appropriate disposal of the effluent as site waste was encouraged. Obstruction of the waterway was not approved. This spill and its impact constitutes a violation of 35 P.S. § 6018.301, 35 P.S. § 691.307(a), * 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), 25 Pa. Code § 102.5(m)4, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e), 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1, 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)1, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.53 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. Violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e) and 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1 were related to the failure of site secondary containment and were shown to have been corrected by the operator prior to the time of inspection. >>A concurrent general surface inspection related to the site ESCGP (ESX16-059-0038) was conducted in response to observed site conditions, particularly multiple slope failures.

Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Veres Well Pad was conducted in response to a report of a spill reported to the Department on 3/22/23 (CTS: 370763).Background:On 3/22/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to regarding a missed call from him the previous evening (3/21/23). Mr. Eighmey informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department hotline. The spill had occurred on the Veres Well Pad. According to Mr. Eighmey, an estimated 30 gallons of brine were released into an earthen containment berm. Greylock was in the process of removing the old tanks at the site to install new tanks with approved secondary containment. Two incidents resulted in the release. A small volume of brine mixed with sand and residual material was released when a manhole cover on the back of a tank was unbolted. Containment was being used at the time, but the volume of fluid mixed with the sediment overflowed out of the containment. Additionally, a vacuum truck was being used to draw down the tanks. The tank on the back of the truck was overfilled. When the suction was turned off, the excess fluid escaped back through the hose and onto the pad. I informed Mr. Eighmey that I would be coming out for a site inspection later the same day (3/22/23).The following was observed during the site inspection:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-A crew was present excavating the spill area (Photo #2). According to Mr. Eighmey, they initially used ground liner containment yesterday to begin remediation efforts (Photo #3). Comments: On March 6, 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to WQS referral in IR 3721238.Access road is heavily saturated in water appearing to cause rutting issues from vehicle traffic. Well is tagged and posted with previous and new operator; pending the transfer currently under review by the Department, the "previous" operator, Questa Petro Co, remains operator at this time according to Department records.While on site, the Department observed active bubbling coming from the top of the well tree shown in Photo 13. Requesting OGI follow up.The leaking of the brine tank identified in IR 3721238 was observed on site shown in Photos 7-8. Specific conductivity readings were recorded as shown in Photos 9-12:- Background: 167.3 uS- On ground below corroded flange: 588 uS- On ground below open line: 820 uS- On ground below valve at well head: 391 uSThese readings indicate that a brine release has occurred on site. The Department recommends removing all impacted soil and properly disposing. The Department requests that the quantity released, composition of fluids released, how the release occurred, and when the release occurred is included in the NOV response. The Department requests disposal documents of the impacted material removed from the site, when made available. Violations issued for brine release.The Department has observed a trend in well sites that are being transferred from Questa Petro Co to Mountain V where the Questa well tags, and associated electrical tape, are being removed and left on site resulting in littering (Photo 4).
